correctness.rationale: Ordinary border implies Abelian border. For a binary word with <=3 occurrences of either bit, if endpoints agree it has a length-one ordinary border; otherwise orient 0...1, let a leading zero run and d final pre-one zero run. If a<=d the literal border 0^a1 exists. If a>d, any disjoint prefix/suffix before left first 1 has fewer 1s than the suffix, and with <=3 ones they cannot each have >=2 ones; hence no Abelian border. For four ones, write 0^a1 0^b1 0^c1 0^d1. Exceptional iff a>d, a+b<=c+d, b!=d; first two enforce an Abelian border with exactly two ones per side and prevent one-one literal border; b!=d excludes the only possible two-one literal border. Reversal covers endpoint 1...0; complementary words covered by sparse rigidity. Parametrize a=d+e,c=b+e+f with e>=1,f>=0,b!=d, yielding 4z^8/((1-z)(1-z^2)^2(1-z^4)), shortest n=8, B_n~n^3/24 and B_n/binom(n,4)~1/n. Independently enumerated all 44,550 words of length <=22 with <=4 ones and checked the mixed-border condition and initial coefficients; proof extends all lengths.
residual_risks: First-exceptional-layer enumeration is only fixed weight four, not all compositions or alphabets.
